Research the applicable law: statutes, subsidiary legislation, judicial decisions, and any persuasive authority (regional or comparative)

Note any factual assumptions that the opinion will rest upon
Summarise research findings in annotated notes for use during drafting
Apply the law to the client's specific facts and instructions
Identify the strongest and weakest aspects of the legal position
Address any assumptions on which the opinion will be based and note where factual confirmation from the client is required
Formulate a clear, definitive conclusion (or a qualified conclusion where the law is uncertain), supported by the legal analysis

State assumptions clearly and limit the opinion to the matters instructed avoid opining on matters outside scope
Use plain, precise language; avoid unnecessary caveats that undermine the utility of the opinion
Ensure the conclusion directly answers the client's question(s)
Senior fee earner or supervising partner reviews the draft for: accuracy of legal analysis, correct citation of authorities, logical consistency, and clarity of conclusions
Confirm that all assumptions and qualifications are appropriate and do not render the opinion unhelpful
Check that the opinion is addressed to the correct party and that its scope matches the original instructions
Revise the draft and obtain internal sign-off before sharing with the client
Share the draft opinion with the client for review
Address any queries or requests for clarification from the client
Where the client raises new factual matters, assess whether these affect the legal analysis and revise accordingly
Confirm that no changes alter the legal conclusions or require a qualification to be added or removed
Incorporate all approved revisions and prepare the final version of the opinion

Confirm the scope of the opinion: identify the specific legal issue, applicable jurisdiction (Rwandan law, regional framework, etc.), and any limitations (e.g. opinion does not cover tax or regulatory matters)
Execute engagement/retainer agreement and confirm fee arrangement
Identify and list all legal issues raised by the instructions
Determine the primary sources to be consulted: legislation, subsidiary legislation, case law, academic commentary, and any relevant regulatory guidance
Assign research tasks to the responsible fee earner(s) and set internal deadlines
Clarify any factual gaps with the client before research begins
Research the applicable law: statutes, subsidiary legislation, judicial decisions, and any persuasive authority (regional or comparative)
Identify any unresolved legal questions, conflicting authorities, or areas of legal uncertainty that will affect the opinion
Note any factual assumptions that the opinion will rest upon
Summarise research findings in annotated notes for use during drafting
Apply the law to the client's specific facts and instructions
Identify the strongest and weakest aspects of the legal position
Address any assumptions on which the opinion will be based and note where factual confirmation from the client is required
Formulate a clear, definitive conclusion (or a qualified conclusion where the law is uncertain), supported by the legal analysis

Draft the opinion in the standard structure: (i) Addressee and date; (ii) Introduction scope and instructions; (iii) Documents and facts considered; (iv) Assumptions and qualifications; (v) Legal analysis by issue; (vi) Conclusion(s)
State assumptions clearly and limit the opinion to the matters instructed avoid opining on matters outside scope
Use plain, precise language; avoid unnecessary caveats that undermine the utility of the opinion
Ensure the conclusion directly answers the client's question(s)
Senior fee earner or supervising partner reviews the draft for: accuracy of legal analysis, correct citation of authorities, logical consistency, and clarity of conclusions
Confirm that all assumptions and qualifications are appropriate and do not render the opinion unhelpful
Check that the opinion is addressed to the correct party and that its scope matches the original instructions
Revise the draft and obtain internal sign-off before sharing with the client
Share the draft opinion with the client for review
Address any queries or requests for clarification from the client
Where the client raises new factual matters, assess whether these affect the legal analysis and revise accordingly
Confirm that no changes alter the legal conclusions or require a qualification to be added or removed
Incorporate all approved revisions and prepare the final version of the opinion
steps.slaText: Within 1 working day of final approval
